questions.statement: Which sentence uses the past simple correctly?
questions.context: Past simple regular verbs, San Juan, grado 11, W03.

options.text: They walked to the beach yesterday.
options.feedback: Correct! 'Walked' is the past simple regular, with the suffix -ed on the stem after a consonant, and 'yesterday' fixes the action in the past.

options.text: They walk to the beach yesterday.
options.feedback: Incorrect! 'walk' is the bare present form, and 'yesterday' can never go with the present.

options.text: They are walked to the beach yesterday.
options.feedback: Incorrect! 'are walked' is not an English form, because the past simple is never built with the auxiliary 'are'.

options.text: They walking to the beach yesterday.
options.feedback: Incorrect! 'walking' is the participle of the progressive, which in the past would need 'were' in front of it.

questions.explanation:
Los verbos regulares forman el pasado simple anadiendo -ed al verbo base. Es el unico tiempo verbal que se construye solo con la raiz del verbo, sin ningun auxiliar, por eso el orden sujeto mas verbo se mantiene intacto.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Complete the sentence: 'We ____ (study) for the exam all last week.'
questions.context: Past simple regular spelling, Ponce, grado 11, W03.

options.feedback: Incorrect! 'Studied' needs one single d at the end, and 'studyed' writes two of them, which no rule allows.
Incorrect! 'study' is the bare present form, and the marker 'all last week' asks for a past action.
Correct! 'Studied' adds the suffix -ed to the stem, and 'all last week' fixes the time in the past.
Incorrect! 'studys' is the present simple of a singular subject, but 'all last week' asks for the past.

questions.explanation:
La ortografia del pasado simple tiene una regla util para los verbos terminados en consonante y -y. En ese caso la -y se cambia por -i y despues se anade -ed, como en 'study' que da 'studied'. Si la vocal anterior es una a, se conserva la -y.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Complete the sentence: 'He ____ (go) to Ponce last Saturday.'
questions.context: Past simple irregular verbs, Carolina, grado 11, W03.

options.feedback: Incorrect! 'goed' treats an irregular verb as a regular one, and the past of 'to go' is a completely different word.
Correct! 'went' is the irregular past simple of the verb 'to go', and it takes no suffix at all.
Incorrect! 'gone' is the past participle, which needs 'have' and describes an action seen from the present.
Incorrect! 'going' is the participle of the progressive, which in the past would need 'was' in front of it.

questions.explanation:
Los verbos irregulares no siguen la regla de anadir -ed y deben aprenderse de memoria. Los mas frecuentes son 'to go', 'to see' y 'to take'. Una forma como 'goed' demuestra que el verbo es irregular y no se puede derivar.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Choose the correct negative: 'I ____ (not / see) the doctor yesterday.'
questions.context: Past simple negative forms, Bayamon, grado 11, W03.

options.feedback: Incorrect! 'didn't saw' puts the past in twice, because the auxiliary 'did' already carries the whole tense.
Incorrect! 'don't see' is a negative in the present, and 'yesterday' points at a finished past time.
Incorrect! 'not saw' has no auxiliary at all, and a negative in the past always needs 'did not'.
Correct! The negative past simple is 'did not' plus the base form, which contracts to 'didn't see'.

questions.explanation:
En pasado simple el negativo se forma siempre con 'did not' o 'didn't', y el verbo principal vuelve a su forma base. Esa es la trampa principal de la unidad: el auxiliar ya marca el pasado, asi que anadir la terminacion del pasado seria incorrecto.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Which question is correct?
questions.context: Past simple questions, Arecibo, grado 11, W03.

options.text: Do you finished the project last week?
options.feedback: Incorrect! 'Do' builds questions in the present, while 'last week' asks for the past simple.

options.text: Did you finished the project last week?
options.feedback: Incorrect! After 'Did' the verb must stay in its base form, and 'finished' keeps a past ending it no longer needs.

options.text: Was you finish the project last week?
options.feedback: Incorrect! 'Was' only works with the verb 'to be', and the main verb of this sentence is the action verb 'to finish'.

options.text: Did you finish the project last week?
options.feedback: Correct! The auxiliary 'Did' opens the question and the main verb returns to the base form 'finish'.

questions.explanation:
Las preguntas de pasado simple se forman con 'did' al principio y el verbo principal en forma base. Igual que en el negativo, el auxiliar ya aporta la marca de pasado y el verbo no la repite. Este patron se repite en todas las preguntas de la unidad.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Complete the sentence: 'They ____ (be) at the party last night.'
questions.context: Past simple with to be, Humacao, grado 11, W03.

options.feedback: Incorrect! 'was' is the singular past of the verb 'to be', and the subject of this sentence is the plural 'they'.
Correct! 'They' is plural, so the past simple of the verb 'to be' here is 'were'.
Incorrect! 'are' is the present of the verb 'to be', and 'last night' points at a finished past time.
Incorrect! 'be' is the bare infinitive, which carries no tense of its own.

questions.explanation:
El pasado simple de 'to be' tiene solo dos formas: 'was' para I, he, she e it, y 'were' para you, we, they. Es el verbo irregular mas frecuente del idioma y aparece en casi todos los ejercicios de pasado.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Which is the correct past simple form of the verb 'to stop'?
questions.context: Past simple spelling rules, Aguadilla, grado 11, W03.

options.feedback: Correct! 'Stop' ends in one consonant after a short vowel, so the double p of the base verb carries over to 'stopped'.
Incorrect! 'stoped' does not double the p, and that double consonant is exactly what the spelling rule requires here.
Incorrect! 'stoppes' is not a form of this verb, because the past simple takes only one suffix.
Incorrect! 'stopt' is not an English form, and no suffix is written after the p in this verb.

questions.explanation:
La duplicacion de consonante en pasado simple ocurre tras vocal breve tensa, como en 'stop' que da 'stopped' o 'plan' que da 'planned'. Si la vocal es larga no se duplica, como en 'look' que da 'looked' o 'call' que da 'called'.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Complete the sentence: 'She ____ (write) three emails last night.'
questions.context: Past simple with irregular verbs, Guayanilla, grado 11, W03.

options.feedback: Incorrect! 'write' is irregular, and simply adding -ed to it produces a word English does not use.
Incorrect! 'written' is the past participle, which needs 'have' rather than a past simple form.
Correct! 'wrote' is the irregular past simple of the verb 'to write', and it is a different word from the base form.
Incorrect! 'write' is the bare present form, and 'last night' fixes the action in the past.

questions.explanation:
El pasado simple irregulares suele terminar en vocal y comparte terminacion con otros verbos. 'To write' y 'to ride' dan 'wrote' y 'rode', mientras que 'to speak' y 'to break' dan 'spoke' y 'broke'. Memorizar las familias completas es mas eficiente que aprenderlas sueltas.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Choose the correct tag: 'He finished the exam, ____?'
questions.context: Past simple question tags, Trujillo Alto, grado 11, W03.

options.feedback: Incorrect! 'doesn't he' is the tag of a present simple clause, and the main verb here is in the past.
Incorrect! 'wasn't he' belongs to the verb 'to be', and the clause uses the action verb 'finished'.
Correct! A tag on a positive past simple clause takes the auxiliary 'did' in its negative form, which gives 'didn't he'.
Incorrect! 'did he not' is the full question form, and a tag is built from the contracted negative.

questions.explanation:
El question tag del pasado simple se construye con 'did' seguido del pronombre y de la forma contracta 'not'. En afirmativo el tag es 'did he' y en negativo es 'didn't he'. El orden siempre es auxiliar, pronombre y negacion.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Complete the sentence: 'They ____ (eat) at the restaurant before the concert.'
questions.context: Past simple with irregular verbs, Barceloneta, grado 11, W03.

options.feedback: Correct! 'Ate' is the irregular past simple of the verb 'to eat', and it takes no suffix at all.
Incorrect! 'eated' adds a regular suffix to an irregular verb, which produces a word English does not use.
Incorrect! 'eaten' is the past participle, which needs 'have' rather than a past simple form.
Incorrect! 'eat' is the bare present form, and 'before the concert' places the action in the past.

questions.explanation:
Los verbos irregulares del pasado tienen tres familias principales. Los terminados en -t como 'eat' dan 'ate', los terminados en -o como 'go' dan 'went' y los terminados en -d como 'build' dan 'built'. Reconocer la familia acelera la memorizacion.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Complete the sentence: 'We ____ (have) a good time at the carnival.'
questions.context: Past simple with to have, Maunabo, grado 11, W03.

options.feedback: Incorrect! 'haved' adds a regular suffix to an irregular verb, and no English form works that way.
Incorrect! 'haveed' gives the verb two suffixes at once, and a verb never carries two endings.
Incorrect! 'hade' writes a single e where English writes 'had', and the past of this verb is irregular.
Correct! 'Had' is the irregular past simple of the verb 'to have', and it carries no suffix.

questions.explanation:
El pasado simple de 'to have' es 'had', y a diferencia de 'to be' no distingue entre singular y plural. Esa misma forma 'had' aparece tambien como auxiliar del pasado perfecto, por lo que conviene reconocer el contexto para no confundirlas.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Complete the sentence: 'It ____ (not / be) cloudy yesterday afternoon.'
questions.context: Past simple with the verb to be, Yauco, grado 11, W03.

options.feedback: Incorrect! 'weren't' is the plural negative of the verb 'to be', and the subject of this sentence is 'it'.
Correct! 'It' is singular, so the negative past simple of the verb 'to be' here is 'wasn't'.
Incorrect! 'didn't' negates an action verb, and the verb of this sentence is the one of 'to be'.
Incorrect! 'isn't' is the negative of the verb 'to be' in the present, and 'yesterday afternoon' is past.

questions.explanation:
El pasado de 'to be' se niega con 'not' detras de la forma 'was' o 'were'. Los auxiliares 'did' no participan nunca con 'to be', porque ese verbo ya es irregular por completo y forma el pasado por sí mismo.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Complete the sentence: 'He ____ (carry) the boxes to the truck.'
questions.context: Past simple with spelling rules, Cayey, grado 11, W03.

options.feedback: Incorrect! 'caried' drops the r before the suffix -ied, but the double r of the base verb must carry over.
Correct! A consonant plus y takes the suffix -ied after doubling the consonant, which gives 'carried'.
Incorrect! 'caryed' keeps the y after the r, and a consonant plus y never takes the plain suffix -ed.
Incorrect! 'carryed' uses the suffix -ed, which English never attaches after a consonant plus y.

questions.explanation:
La -y del pasado simple se convierte en -i solo cuando la consonante o vocal anterior no es una 'a'. Si la -y va precedida de vocal larga se conserva, como en 'play' que da 'played' o 'enjoy' que da 'enjoyed'.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Complete the sentence: 'The committee ____ (decide) the date last Tuesday.'
questions.context: Past simple with irregular verbs, San Sebastian, grado 11, W03.

options.feedback: Incorrect! 'Decidded' doubles a d that this verb never doubles, so the suffix is a plain -ed.
Incorrect! 'Decied' drops the d before the suffix -ied, but English always keeps it after a consonant.
Incorrect! 'decidedd' writes the suffix twice, and a verb never carries two endings.
Correct! 'Decided' takes the plain suffix -ed after the vowel i, with no doubling and no change of the y.

questions.explanation:
Cuando el verbo ya termina en -e o en -d, el pasado simple solo necesita la -d del sufijo. Asi 'decide' da 'decided', 'like' da 'liked' y 'need' da 'needed'. No hay que duplicar nada en estos casos.

questions.statement: Complete the sentence: 'I ____ (do) my homework before dinner yesterday.'
questions.context: Past simple with the verb to do, Camuy, grado 11, W03.

options.feedback: Incorrect! 'doed' adds a regular suffix to an irregular verb, which produces a word English does not use.
Incorrect! 'done' is the past participle, which needs 'have' rather than a past simple auxiliary.
Correct! 'Did' is the irregular past simple of the verb 'to do', and it doubles as the auxiliary of the tense.
Incorrect! 'do' is the bare present form, and 'before dinner yesterday' fixes the action in the past.

questions.explanation:
'To do' es uno de los verbos irregulares mas usados y su pasado simple es 'did'. Conviene no confundirlo con 'done', que es el participio pasado. La diferencia se ve en el auxiliar: solo el pasado usa 'did' como verbo principal.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Question: 'Did you call the doctor?' Answer: '____'
questions.context: Past simple in short answers, Luquillo, grado 11, W03.

options.feedback: Correct! 'Yes, I did' repeats the auxiliary of the question and adds nothing else, which is the standard short answer.
Incorrect! 'Yes, I was' uses the wrong auxiliary, because the question was built with 'Did'.
Incorrect! 'Yes, I called' adds a new piece of information, and a short answer only agrees with the question.
Incorrect! 'Yes, I do' uses the auxiliary of the present, and 'Did' already carried the past tense.

questions.explanation:
Las respuestas cortas en pasado simple usan el mismo auxiliar que la pregunta. Como la pregunta abre con 'did', la respuesta abre con 'did' y el verbo principal se omite. Ese es el criterio para elegir entre 'did', 'was' y 'do'.

questions.statement: Complete the sentence: 'They ____ (break) the window when the ball hit it.'
questions.context: Past simple with irregular verbs, Toa Baja, grado 11, W03.

options.feedback: Correct! 'broke' is the irregular past simple of the verb 'to break', and it is written with an o.
Incorrect! 'breaked' adds a regular suffix to an irregular verb, and no English form works that way.
Incorrect! 'broken' is the past participle, which needs 'have' rather than a past simple form.
Incorrect! 'break' is the bare present form, and the clause describes an action finished in the past.

questions.explanation:
La terminacion -oke del pasado irregular es muy productiva. La comparten 'to break', 'to speak', 'to drive', 'to wake' y 'to choose'. Identificar la familia evita tener que memorizar cada verbo por separado.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Complete the sentence: 'The students ____ (take) the exam on Monday morning.'
questions.context: Past simple with irregular verbs, Naguabo, grado 11, W03.

options.feedback: Incorrect! 'takeed' adds a regular suffix to an irregular verb, and no English form works that way.
Incorrect! 'taken' is the past participle, which needs 'have' rather than a past simple auxiliary.
Incorrect! 'taked' adds the suffix -ed, but the past of 'to take' is irregular and takes no suffix.
Correct! 'took' is the irregular past simple of the verb 'to take', a completely different word.

questions.explanation:
Varios verbos irregulares forman su pasado con una vocal larga en lugar de terminacion. 'To take' da 'took', 'to speak' da 'spoke' y 'to break' da 'broke'. Son las formas que mas errores producen por parecerse a las del presente.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Which sentence uses the past simple of the verb 'to be' correctly?
questions.context: Past simple with the verb to be, Hatillo, grado 11, W03.

options.text: She didn't ready for the test.
options.feedback: Incorrect! 'didn't ready' puts the auxiliary 'did' in front of an adjective, and no English clause allows that.

options.text: She wasn't ready for the test.
options.feedback: Correct! 'wasn't' is the negative past of the verb 'to be', and it is followed by the adjective 'ready'.

options.text: She wasn't be ready for the test.
options.feedback: Incorrect! After the auxiliary 'wasn't' the base form 'be' can never follow, so this is not an English form.

options.text: She isn't ready for the test yesterday.
options.feedback: Incorrect! 'isn't' is the negative of the verb 'to be' in the present, and 'yesterday' points at the past.

questions.explanation:
Con 'to be' el pasado simple es 'was' o 'were' y no lleva auxiliar 'did' delante. El verbo 'to be' tiene su propio sistema de pasado, por eso un adjetivo como 'ready' se coloca directamente despues sin ninguna forma verbal adicional.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Which sentence is correct?
questions.context: Past simple with prepositions of time, Yabucoa, grado 11, W03.

options.text: She moves to Mayaguez two years ago.
options.feedback: Incorrect! 'moves' is the simple present of a singular subject, and 'two years ago' asks for the past.

options.text: She is moving to Mayaguez two years ago.
options.feedback: Incorrect! 'is moving' is the present continuous, which wants a marker such as 'right now' instead of a past one.

options.text: She moved to Mayaguez two years ago.
options.feedback: Correct! 'Moved' is the past simple regular, and 'two years ago' fixes the action in a finished past time.

options.text: She moved to Mayaguez two years ago tomorrow.
options.feedback: Incorrect! 'tomorrow' points at the future, and a clause about the past cannot end with it.

questions.explanation:
Las expresiones de tiempo guian la eleccion del tiempo verbal. 'Ago', 'yesterday' y 'last' exigen pasado simple, mientras que 'tomorrow' y 'next week' piden futuro. Reconocer la marca antes de conjugar evita la mayoria de los errores de esta unidad.
